children: Morgan Stanley updated investors on Friday that Tesla
has become a credible emerging competitor in the autonomous trucking sector.

Analyst Andrew Percoco highlighted that the Tesla Semi itself is finally moving toward higher-volume production, with a rollout expected this year. "More importantly, CEO Elon Musk provided a timeline for offering the self-driving Tesla Semi, expecting the capability by 2027 ahead of scaled production of the Semi," wrote Percoco. "We have long considered TSLA to be a potential wildcard in the competitive landscape of AV trucking, and this timeline provides more definitive evidence of their plans to enter the market in earnest," he added.

Autonomous trucking was noted to offer 2.3X better utilization, 20% lower cost per mile, and 6X higher profit per truck in comparison to human driving. The rise of diesel prices to over $6 per gallon in the U.S. was also highlighted as a dramatic point supporting the Tesla

Putting pen to paper, Percoco and his team calculated that Tesla can generate ~$12K to $18K per month from its autonomous trucking software using an estimated $0.85 to $1.00 per mile subscription fee times 18K miles driven per month.
Morgan Stanley has a price target of $400 on Tesla
and a new bull case scenario PT of $840.
The Tesla Semi could be a long-term competitive threat to a long list of trucking-related stocks, including Knight-Swift Transportation

title: Do $6 diesel fuel prices open up the fast lane for the Tesla Semi?
